change.author: Gabe Villalobos

findings.title: `queued` default is evaluated once at import time
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a dataclass default. Python evaluates it once, when the module is imported. Every `AssignmentSource` built without an explicit `queued` gets the same timestamp: the process start time. `from_integration` never passes `queued`. The value that `to_dict()` sends in the task kwargs is therefore stale, and it is identical across all assignments in a worker. Nothing reads it yet, but it is wrong for any later use such as ordering or staleness checks. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead.

findings.title: test_to_dict cannot catch the import-time `queued` default
findings.body: `assert result.get("queued") is not None` passes even when `queued` is a stale import-time value. Add an assertion that `queued` is fresh, for example that it is no earlier than a timestamp taken just before constructing the source. Such a test would have caught the default-argument bug at assignment_source.py:18.

findings.title: Loop-prevention is only tested for assign via GroupAssignee.objects.assign
findings.body: The new code adds `assignment_source` to `deassign` too, and `sync_group_assignee_inbound` passes `AssignmentSource.from_integration(integration)` on both paths. The only test of the source check is the `assign` case in `test_assignee_sync_outbound_assign_with_matching_source_integration`. No test covers `deassign` with a matching source. No test covers `sync_group_assignee_inbound` forwarding the source. No test covers a non-matching source integration still syncing, which the code comment says should happen. A regression in the `deassign` or inbound wiring would go unnoticed.

contracts.action: Outbound assignee sync is skipped when the assignment source is the same integration
contracts.equivalent_path: src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_status_outbound.py:43 calls should_sync("outbound_status") with no source. Status sync has no loop guard here.
contracts.before_after: Before, should_sync only checked the org-integration config flag. Now it also returns False when sync_source.integration_id equals org_integration.integration_id. The source is built in utils/sync.py:98 and 115, passed through assign/deassign (groupassignee.py:192 and 238), serialized into the Celery kwargs (utils/sync.py:137-144), and parsed in the task (tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py:53-56).
contracts.visible_effect: An inbound assignment from Jira/VSTS no longer echoes back to the same integration. Other integrations linked to the same group still receive the change.
contracts.failure_mode: If from_dict fails, the source becomes None and the sync proceeds, so the loop guard is lost silently. The `queued` default is stale because it is evaluated at import time, though nothing reads it yet. All implementations of sync_assignee_outbound accept **kwargs, so passing assignment_source does not raise.

summary: The loop-guard wiring is sound end to end, and every `sync_assignee_outbound` implementation accepts `**kwargs`. I found one real bug: `AssignmentSource.queued` defaults to `timezone.now()` evaluated once at import, so it is stale. Two test gaps remain: nothing asserts `queued` is fresh, and the `deassign` and inbound paths have no coverage.
